life_summary: William Smith was born March 13, 1811, in Royalton, Vermont, the eighth child of Joseph Smith Sr. and Lucy Mack Smith. He grew up in a financially struggling household and received minimal formal education. The family's economic hardship shaped much of his early life, though he was baptized into the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints on June 9, 1830, by David Whitmer. Smith worked in various capacities throughout his life, including civic service in Illinois. He eventually settled in Iowa, where he spent his final years. Smith's life was marked by significant ecclesiastical advancement in his youth followed by a dramatic and controversial fall from authority.
church_summary: William Smith was ordained an apostle on February 15, 1835, after his brother Joseph insisted on his selection despite objections from other church leaders. Following Hyrum Smith's death in 1844, William succeeded him as Presiding Patriarch in 1845. However, he encountered significant conflict with Brigham Young over the scope of his patriarchal authority. After expressing strong disagreement with church leadership, comparing Young to Pontius Pilate and Nero and accusing leaders of plural marriage practices, Smith was excommunicated on October 19, 1845. Rather than following Young to Utah, he initially affiliated with James J. Strang's Strangite movement and later joined the Reorganized Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints in 1878, remaining a high priest until his death.
